mismatches.status: LATENT — searchArticles has no caller; this breaks the moment it gets one
mismatches.actual: A flat 34-key article × company × exchange JOIN row. There is no `companies` array and no `images` array at all; the single company is inlined as `companyId`/`companyName`/`logoFileName`, and the exchange listing is inlined as `exchangeIdent`/`tickerId`/`bloombergCode`/`reutersCode`/`yahooCode`/`googleCode`/`financialContentCode`.
mismatches.impact: `mapArticleListItem` opens with `api.companies.map(...)`. On a search row `companies` is undefined, so the first call throws a TypeError. Nothing calls it today, which is the only reason this has not been seen.
mismatches.fix: Declare a separate `ApiArticleSearchItem` and a `mapArticleSearchItem`, or normalise search rows into the list shape at the endpoint boundary. Do NOT keep the current declaration — it is the single most misleading type in the folder.

mismatches.expected: ApiArticleFeedItem, carrying `sectorName` and no `language` — the same shape as homepage and by-industry.
mismatches.actual: The AP-DETAIL shape. `sectorName` is ABSENT; `language`, `sectors`, `bodyHtml`, `bodyText`, `subHeadLine`, `topicName` and `sourceName` are all present and undeclared. `sectors` is [] on every row and `sourceName` is null on every row, so neither substitutes for the missing `sectorName`.
mismatches.impact: `mapArticleFeedItem` reads `str(api.sectorName)` → null → `mapClassification([])` → sector_type null, industries [], classification_overridden false. Every release in a company feed would land unclassified, while `language` — which IS on the wire — is thrown away.
mismatches.fix: Three endpoints, two shapes: type by-company off the press-release shape (it is the same row), keep ApiArticleFeedItem for homepage and by-industry, and read `language` where it exists.

mismatches.expected: Absent. repository.ts:566 — "The detail endpoint carries the body but not the language, and the list row carries the language but not the body, so the language is threaded in from" the cached list row: `const language = cached?.languages[0] ?? null`.
mismatches.actual: The detail endpoint DOES return `language` — "EN", "ZH-CN", "ZH-TW", "KO" across 13 samples. It is an undeclared key on ApiPressRelease.
mismatches.impact: Opening an article whose list row is not in the cache — a direct URL visit, a cold cache, a cleared IndexedDB — loses the language and the editor falls back to createArticle's default of English. The correct value was in the response the whole time. Mapping it directly also removes the coupling between loadArticleRecord and the list cache.
mismatches.fix: Add `language: string | null` to ApiPressRelease and read `options.language ?? api.language` in mapPressRelease. One line each, no behaviour change when the cache is warm.

mismatches.expected: endpoints.ts documents `SecId` as "a sector id from lib/sectors.ts", `Cid` as "a company id", `ArtType` as "the server's ArtType. No enumeration of the values is published."
mismatches.actual: SecId and ArtType are IGNORED — SecId=186 and ArtType=1 each return the byte-identical id sequence to an unfiltered call (110114, 110113, 110112, 110106, 110108). Cid is NOT a company id: 82, 574 and 9453 all return [], while 2, 3, 4 and 5 each return a distinct non-empty set — the same small numbers that appear as `sourceId` on article rows. Only HasThumbnail actually filters.
mismatches.impact: Any list filter built on SecId or ArtType silently returns unfiltered data — the worst failure mode, because it looks like it worked. A "filter by company" built on Cid returns nothing for every real company id.
mismatches.fix: Do not expose SecId/ArtType as filters. Filter by company via /by-company/{id} once AP-M2 is settled. Correct the Cid comment to "a source/wire id (2 = ACN, 3 = JCN)" — or confirm with the API team, since a parameter named Cid behaving as a source id is more likely a backend bug than a naming choice.

mismatches.expected: "`industry` matches a `sector_name`" — a value from lib/sectors.ts.
mismatches.actual: Only 4 of the 75 sector_names in lib/sectors.ts return rows (Automotive, Food & Beverage, BioTech, Trade Shows). What the endpoint actually matches is the article's own coarse `sectorName`, whose observed value space is Business, Healthcare, Technology, Industrial, Automotive — and three of those five are sector_TYPE values in the master list, not sector_names.
mismatches.impact: An industry filter driven from the app's sector list would come back empty for 71 of 75 options. This is the THIRD taxonomy in play: press-release `sectors[]` uses fine-grained names ("Enterprise IT", "Healthcare & Pharm"), article `sectorName` uses the coarse set, and lib/sectors.ts has its own ids. See AC-M1 for the id half of the same problem.
mismatches.fix: Drive the filter from the coarse `sectorName` values observed on the wire, not from lib/sectors.ts. Longer term this needs one taxonomy agreed with the API team.

mismatches.expected: `hasImage: boolean` — whether the article has an image. `imageUrl: string | null`.
mismatches.actual: Over 100 consecutive list rows: `hasImage` was false on 100/100 while 28 of them carried a non-empty `images[]`. `imageUrl` was null on 100/100 — never populated on any row of any endpoint sampled.
mismatches.impact: `hasImage` is not a usable signal; `images.length > 0` is. `imageUrl` is dead weight in the type. Note the contrast: the `HasThumbnail=true` QUERY parameter works correctly, so the server can tell which articles have images — it just does not say so in this field.
mismatches.fix: Branch on `images.length`, never on `hasImage`. Mark `imageUrl` as never-populated in types.ts rather than deleting it, since it is in the wire response.

mismatches.actual: /api/Articles past the last page returns 200 with []. /api/Articles/by-company past the last page returns 404. /api/Articles/search ignores Page entirely (Page=2 → [] at any Size).
mismatches.impact: A shared paging helper has to treat a 404 as end-of-list for one endpoint and as a real error for another. repository.ts's sweep stops on a short page, which handles the [] case; a 404 currently surfaces as an ApiError.

mismatches.expected: endpoints.ts: "returned `[]` on the dev host when sampled."
mismatches.actual: Returns 50 rows (30 with hasThumbnail=true), matching ApiArticleFeedItem exactly.
mismatches.impact: None — but the comment would stop someone building on a working endpoint.

mismatches.field: sectors, topicName, body, sourceId→sourceName, language tags
mismatches.expected: `sectors: string[]` (a real array); `topicName` a constant section label, deliberately not mapped to `topic`; `body` null with `bodyHtml` carrying the markup; sourceId 2 = ACN, 3 = JCN; wire language tags ZH-CN/ZH-TW mapped to ZH-HANS/ZH-HANT.
mismatches.actual: All five confirmed across 13 press-release samples and 100 list rows. `sectors` is a real JSON array (NOT the JSON-encoded string the public site's code expects — this repo has it right). `topicName` is "Press release summary" on all 13. `body` is null on all 13. Only sourceIds 2 and 3 were observed. Languages observed: EN, JA, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, KO — all five are in LANGUAGE_BY_API_TAG.
mismatches.impact: No action. Recorded because these are the assumptions most likely to be doubted during unification, and because the public site's repo is WRONG about `sectors` where this one is right.
